== Synopsis ==

Bored upon a riverbank, Alice finds herself captivated by the sight of a remarkable White Rabbit carrying a pocket watch. Overcome with curiosity, she abandons her reverie and follows the creature out of impulse, only to tumble headlong down a rabbit-hole. She falls through a deep well, her mind turning to geographic calculations and the distance of her descent, as the peculiar adventure begins in earnest.

Upon landing, Alice discovers herself caught in a strange progression of transformations. She grows to nine feet in height, her body stretching whilst she contemplates the oddity of her changing form. Her distress becomes so acute that she weeps with such intensity as to create a large pool of tears surrounding her in the hall where she finds herself. When the White Rabbit briefly appears, carrying gloves and a fan, he takes fright at the sight of her and flees in alarm.

Encounters with other inhabitants of this topsy-turvy realm follow in swift succession. Alice gathers with animals wet from the tears, where the Mouse proposes reciting history to dry them all. She comes to grieve over having mentioned Dinah, a name that sets the Mouse to anger, causing him to depart in a huff. Alice then discovers herself in the Rabbit's own house, where she finds an unlabeled bottle near a looking glass. Her enlargement within the house forces her escape, and she is pursued by an enormous puppy before finding refuge in the woods. When the Rabbit's companions attempt to extract her, Alice's kicks send a creature named Bill tumbling down the chimney.

In the woods, Alice encounters the Caterpillar, whose indifferent manner frustrates her greatly. When she complains of her diminished height—reduced to three inches—the Caterpillar, being precisely that height himself, declares it a perfectly good height and assures her she will adjust in time. Through the use of her mushroom, she returns briefly to her normal stature before shrinking once more to nine inches, cautiously approaching a small house to avoid alarming its occupants. This is the peculiar dwelling of the March Hare, which boasts ear-shaped chimneys and a roof of fur. Here, she witnesses the Cheshire Cat vanish and reappear, confirming the mysterious transformation of a baby into a pig. Alice herself discovers she holds this pig-creature and, realizing its transformation, releases it into the woods.

Leaving a chaotic tea party in disgust, Alice finds a door set within a tree that leads her back to the garden. There she rejoins the March Hare and Hatter, claiming there is no room at their table despite its considerable size. The Hatter reveals a quarrel with Time itself during a Queen of Hearts concert, leaving him unable to control it any longer. The Queen then summons Alice to join her in a chaotic croquet game played with live hedgehogs and flamingoes. The Queen sentences the gardeners to execution, only for Alice to rescue them in a flower-pot. When the Queen's grand procession arrives at the garden, Alice makes the defiant choice not to bow.

The Queen's cruelty knows no bounds. She forces Alice to continue their croquet game whilst ordering the execution of the other players. The Queen directs Alice to meet the Mock Turtle and hear his life story. Whilst recounting her adventures to the assembled creatures, Alice mentions that the words she recited to the Caterpillar came out different than she remembered, a claim that intrigues the Mock Turtle greatly. He describes to her with considerable emotion the Lobster Quadrille, a dance of complex steps involving seals, turtles, and lobsters as dancing partners.

At the trial of the Knave of Hearts, accused of stealing the Queen's tarts, Alice finds herself growing larger as the proceedings unfold. She disputes with the Dormouse about the reasonableness of her growth, even as the trial descends into chaos. The Queen orders the Dormouse removed, and the cook vanishes before examination can begin. In her growing agitation, Alice accidentally upsets the jury-box with her skirt, scattering the jurymen across the floor. She then defies the court entirely, challenging their illogic and declaring them to be nothing but a pack of cards. The cards rise up and descend upon her in a tumultuous fall, and Alice awakens on the riverbank, cradled in her sister's lap.
